correctness.rationale: For every nonempty finite preorder and arbitrary modal relation, upward-normalize each row without changing any formula. Nonprincipal finite upsets split into two proper upsets. For sufficiency, a hypothetical failed di instance has a witness t in a row covered by A union B but outside C; PR supplies a principal future subrow, which must lie in A or B, contradicting the strict premises. For necessity, choose a minimal t-containing subrow when PR fails, split it into two proper upsets A,B, and let C be the complement of the downset of t. Any future row inside A or B and outside C would strictly shrink the chosen minimal row. This explicitly refutes di. The 3-world directedness-separating example and 2-world minimality are checked analytically. A standalone checker exhaustively agrees with direct semantics on 14,914 labelled raw frames through 3 worlds and samples 600 four-world frames; enumeration is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: An explicit 2026 flat-frame article obtains sharp logic through a sufficient downward-directed subclass. The present condition completely classifies all finite frames validating the sharpening axiom, supplies explicit negative valuations, identifies a strict 3-world separating model, and gives a polynomial decision procedure. It is a natural logical-frame correspondence gap, not a routine finite enumeration, arbitrary parameter choice, or rephrasing of an algebraic axiom.
